title: HTTP 400 Bad Request
problem: The external API rejects the request because the request body, query parameters, or headers are malformed or structurally invalid. This is distinct from HTTP 422, which accepts the structure but rejects the data values.
symptoms: Module fails with HTTP 400 status
API error response body contains field-specific or structure-specific messages
Error happens consistently for specific data or after a configuration change
Error occurs immediately after a mapping change

likely_causes.cause: A required request parameter is missing from the body or query string
The request body is malformed or not valid JSON when JSON is expected
A field value does not match the expected format for this specific API
An unexpected or unknown field is included in the request body

diagnosis_steps: Open the failing execution and read the full error response body from the HTTP module — it typically contains specific field error messages
Identify which field or parameter the API is rejecting based on the error body
Compare the request sent by Make with the API documentation for that specific endpoint
Reproduce the same request in Postman or curl with the exact same data to isolate whether the issue is in the data or in how Make sends it
Determine whether the error occurs for all records or only specific ones — if data-dependent, inspect the failing record's field values

solutions.solution: Read the full 400 error response body to identify the exact rejected field or structure issue, then correct the specific mapping or parameter
solutions.conditions: General first step — the specific correction depends entirely on what the error body reports

solutions.solution: Add missing required parameters by mapping the correct field from the source module or by setting a static default value
solutions.conditions: When the error body indicates a missing required parameter

solutions.solution: Validate the JSON body by using parseJSON() on the body string and inspecting the result in a test run
solutions.conditions: When the request body may be malformed due to incorrect string concatenation or encoding

prevention: Always read the full error response body — it usually contains the exact field causing the 400
Test API endpoints manually with representative sample data before building the Make scenario
Add validation filters before HTTP modules to ensure required fields are present before sending the request

origin_details.evidence: HTTP 400 is a standard HTTP status code well-defined in RFC 7231. The behavior in Make's HTTP module is consistent with standard HTTP semantics. Specific error messages are generic and vary by API — not from a single confirmed source. Solutions are logically sound but context-dependent.

title: HTTP 401 Unauthorized — authentication failure from external API
problem: The external API returns 401 because Make's request does not include valid authentication credentials. This is an error from the external service — Make is correctly forwarding the credentials stored in the connection, but those credentials are rejected by the external API.
symptoms: Module fails immediately with 401 status on every execution
Error started occurring after a period where the scenario was working
Error started after a password change or account modification on the external service
All modules using the same connection fail simultaneously

likely_causes.cause: OAuth2 access token stored by Make has expired and the refresh token is also invalid or expired
The user changed their password on the external service, invalidating all OAuth tokens
API key has been deleted, rotated, or deactivated on the external service
The OAuth2 app access was revoked by the user in the external service's settings

diagnosis_steps: Go to Make > Connections and find the connection used by the failing module
Check the connection status — a warning icon or error indicator shows an issue
Attempt to reauthorize the connection
If using an API Key, verify that the key is still active in the external service's dashboard
Check if the OAuth2 scopes granted to Make are still valid
Look for recent account changes on the external service (password change, permission revocation)

solutions.solution: Go to Make > Connections > find the failing connection > click Reauthorize and complete the OAuth2 flow
solutions.conditions: When the OAuth2 token has expired or the refresh token is invalid

solutions.solution: Delete the failing connection and create a new one with fresh credentials
solutions.conditions: When Reauthorize fails or the connection is in an unrecoverable broken state

solutions.solution: Generate a new API key in the external service dashboard and update the Make connection with it
solutions.conditions: When using API key authentication and the key was rotated or deleted

prevention: Use dedicated service accounts rather than personal accounts for Make connections to avoid disruption from password changes
Set up Make scenario failure notifications to catch 401 errors immediately
Regularly audit connections in Make > Connections to verify their status

title: HTTP 403 Forbidden — insufficient permissions on external API
problem: The external API accepts the authentication credentials but rejects the request because the authenticated account or token does not have permission to perform the requested action on the requested resource.
symptoms: Module fails with 403 after what appears to be successful authentication
Error occurs for specific resources or actions but not others
Error started after a role or permission change in the external service
Error is consistent — not data-dependent

likely_causes.cause: The connected account does not have the required role or permission level in the external service
The OAuth2 scope granted to Make does not include the required permission for this specific action
The API plan or subscription tier does not include access to the requested endpoint
The resource being accessed is owned by a different user or workspace and the account cannot access it

diagnosis_steps: Read the full 403 error response body — it often specifies which permission or scope is missing
Check the role and permissions of the account used for the Make connection in the external service's admin panel
Review the OAuth2 scopes granted during the Make connection authorization — compare with the API documentation for the required scope for this action
Verify whether the resource being accessed requires admin-level access or a specific role

solutions.solution: Grant the required permissions to the connected account in the external service, then reauthorize the Make connection
solutions.conditions: When the account lacks the required role (e.g., not admin, wrong team role)

solutions.solution: Delete the Make connection and recreate it, ensuring that all required OAuth2 scopes for the needed actions are granted during the authorization step
solutions.conditions: When scopes were not granted during initial authorization and cannot be added without re-authorization

prevention: Before creating a Make connection, review the required permissions for each module and action in the API documentation
Grant only the scopes required by the specific modules and actions used in the workflow — not broader than needed
Use accounts with the appropriate role level for Make integrations

title: HTTP 404 Not Found — resource does not exist on external service
problem: The HTTP module or integration module targets a resource (record, file, endpoint URL) that does not exist on the external service. The 404 response is from the external service.
symptoms: Module fails with 404 on specific records but not others
A hardcoded ID in the scenario refers to a deleted or non-existent resource
The resource existed during development but was deleted before the scenario ran in production

likely_causes.cause: A hardcoded record ID in the module points to a resource that has since been deleted
A dynamically mapped ID is incorrect or refers to a non-existent resource
The API endpoint URL contains a typo or incorrect path segment
The resource exists in a different environment (staging vs production) than the one being called

diagnosis_steps: Open the failing execution and inspect the exact URL sent by the HTTP module including all path segments and the resource ID
Verify directly in the external service whether that resource exists
Determine whether the ID is hardcoded or dynamically mapped — if dynamic, trace where the ID originates and verify it is correct
Verify the API endpoint URL structure against the current official API documentation

solutions.solution: Add an Error Handler on the failing module to gracefully handle 404 responses (log the missing ID, skip the record, or send an alert notification)
solutions.conditions: When 404s are expected to occur sometimes and should not stop the entire scenario

solutions.solution: Replace hardcoded resource IDs with dynamic mappings sourced from upstream data
solutions.conditions: When a hardcoded ID caused the 404 by pointing to a deleted or wrong resource

solutions.solution: Add a lookup or search step before the action module to verify the resource exists before attempting to update or delete it
solutions.conditions: When the resource may have been deleted between the trigger and the action

prevention: Never hardcode resource IDs in production scenarios — always map them dynamically from upstream data
Add Error Handlers for 404 responses on modules that modify or read specific records

title: HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity — data validation failure
problem: The external API understands the request format (unlike 400) but rejects it because the data values fail the API's validation rules. Common causes include missing required fields, wrong formats, invalid enum values, or type mismatches in the request data.
symptoms: Module fails with 422 — data was received by the API but rejected
Error response body contains per-field validation messages
Error is data-dependent — fails for some records but not others
Error occurs after a mapping change or when new types of records are processed

likely_causes.cause: A required field in the API request is empty or null for this record
A field value does not match the expected format (date format, phone format, email format, enum value)
A field type is wrong (string passed where integer expected, or vice versa)
An enum field receives a value not in the API's accepted list
The mapping is correct for most records but the source field is absent for some edge cases

diagnosis_steps: Open the failing execution and read the full 422 response body — it should identify the specific fields that failed validation
Map each field error in the response to the corresponding Make module field mapping
Inspect the actual value that was sent for each failing field
Check the API documentation for the exact validation rules for each field (required, format, enum values, length limits)
Test the request in Postman with the exact same data Make sent to confirm the issue is in the data values

solutions.solution: When required field is empty: use ifempty() to provide a default value, or add a filter before the module to skip records where the required field is absent
solutions.conditions: When the 422 response body indicates a required field is missing or empty

solutions.solution: When date format is wrong: use formatDate() to convert to the exact format the API requires (verify the required format in the API documentation)
solutions.conditions: When the 422 response body indicates a date field has an invalid format

solutions.solution: When an enum field is invalid: create a mapping table using if() or a Set Variables module to convert source values to the API's accepted enum values
solutions.conditions: When the source system uses different labels than the target API's enum values

solutions.solution: When a type mismatch: use toNumber(), toString(), or parseNumber() to convert the value to the correct type before sending
solutions.conditions: When the 422 indicates a type mismatch (string vs integer, etc.)

prevention: Always read the target API documentation for each endpoint's field validation rules before building the scenario
Test with edge-case data (empty fields, unusual value formats) during development before deploying
Add data validation (filters plus Set Variables) before API modules to detect invalid values early

title: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests — rate limit from external API
problem: Make sends requests to an external API faster than the API's rate limit allows. The API returns 429. This is an error from the external service — Make is sending valid requests but too frequently for the API's policy.
symptoms: Module fails consistently when processing large volumes via an Iterator
Error is intermittent at moderate volumes but consistent at high volumes
API error response may contain a Retry-After header
Multiple Make scenarios calling the same API all fail together

likely_causes.cause: An Iterator is processing records without delay and exceeds the API's requests-per-minute limit
Multiple Make scenarios calling the same API simultaneously exceed the combined rate limit
The current API plan tier has a lower rate limit than needed for the processing volume

diagnosis_steps: Read the 429 error response body — it may include rate limit details (requests per minute, reset time)
Check the Retry-After header value in the response — it indicates how many seconds to wait
Calculate how many API calls the scenario makes per minute at the current volume
Compare with the API's documented rate limit for the current plan tier
Check whether multiple scenarios are calling the same API and add their request rates together

solutions.solution: Add a Tools > Sleep module inside the Iterator loop to introduce a delay between each API call. The minimum safe delay is: 60000ms divided by the API's requests-per-minute limit
solutions.conditions: When an Iterator without delay is the direct cause of the rate limit being exceeded

solutions.solution: Add an Error Handler on the rate-limited module with retry logic that waits for the Retry-After duration before retrying
solutions.conditions: When 429 errors are intermittent and automatic retry after waiting is acceptable

solutions.solution: Consolidate multiple scenarios calling the same API into a single scenario to reduce total parallel request volume
solutions.conditions: When multiple scenarios are collectively exceeding the rate limit

solutions.solution: Use a batch endpoint if the API supports it to send multiple records in one request instead of one request per record
solutions.conditions: When the API offers a batch insert or batch update endpoint

prevention: Calculate the theoretical API call rate before deploying any Iterator-based scenario that calls an external API
Add a Sleep module with a delay calculated from the API rate limit inside any Iterator that calls an external API in each iteration

origin_details.evidence: HTTP 429 semantics defined by RFC 6585. Sleep module confirmed in Make documentation. title: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error from external service
problem: The external API returns a 500 error indicating a server-side failure on the API provider's infrastructure. This is not a Make error and is not caused by the request data. Make surfaces it as a module failure.
symptoms: Module fails with 500 status
Error is typically intermittent — not caused by specific data values
Error correlates with external service incidents or high-load periods
Retrying the same execution often succeeds

likely_causes.cause: The external service is experiencing a transient infrastructure failure or is under high load
The external service has a bug triggered by specific data combinations in the request

diagnosis_steps: Check the external service's official status page for ongoing incidents
Wait a few minutes and manually retry the incomplete execution
Determine whether the error reproduces consistently with the same data (suggests a service-side data bug) or is random (transient failure)
If consistent, test the exact same request in Postman to confirm it is a service-side issue

solutions.solution: Add an Error Handler with a Repeater (3-5 retries with increasing delay) to automatically retry on 500 errors
solutions.conditions: When 500 errors are transient and the external service normally recovers within minutes

solutions.solution: Store incomplete executions and reprocess them manually once the external service recovers
solutions.conditions: When the 500 is caused by a known service incident and manual reprocessing is acceptable

solutions.solution: Report the issue to the external service's support team with the request details if the 500 reproduces consistently with specific data
solutions.conditions: When the same request data consistently triggers a 500 response (service bug)

prevention: Add Error Handlers with retry logic on all HTTP modules calling external APIs
Subscribe to status pages of critical external services used in your scenarios

title: HTTP 503 Service Unavailable — external service down
problem: The external service is temporarily unavailable due to maintenance, overload, or a platform outage. Make's module receives a 503 and fails. This is not a Make error.
symptoms: Multiple modules or scenarios calling the same external service all fail simultaneously
Error coincides with an entry on the external service's status page
Error resolves on its own after a period (service recovery)

likely_causes.cause: External service is experiencing a planned or unplanned outage
External service is temporarily overloaded and rejecting new requests

diagnosis_steps: Check the external service's official status page for any active incidents
Verify whether all Make scenarios calling this service are failing simultaneously — confirms a service-wide issue rather than a data or configuration problem
Wait for the service to recover before reprocessing incomplete executions

solutions.solution: Store incomplete executions and reprocess them manually after the external service has recovered
solutions.conditions: When the 503 is caused by a service outage and manual reprocessing is the appropriate approach

solutions.solution: Add an Error Handler with retry logic using a longer delay interval (e.g., retry after several minutes)
solutions.conditions: When brief outages are expected for this service and automated retry after a delay is acceptable

prevention: Subscribe to status pages of critical external services
Enable incomplete execution storage for scenarios that depend on external services to allow reprocessing after recovery

title: HTTP 413 Payload Too Large
problem: The request body sent by Make exceeds the size limit of the external API or the Make platform. Commonly occurs when uploading files, sending large JSON bodies, or transmitting base64-encoded content.
symptoms: File upload module fails for large files but succeeds for small files
HTTP module fails when sending a large JSON body
Error occurs when transmitting base64-encoded images or documents

likely_causes.cause: File or payload size exceeds the target API's documented maximum payload limit
Base64-encoded file content is embedded directly in JSON body instead of being uploaded as a file reference
Large API response content is being forwarded as a request body without size reduction

diagnosis_steps: Check the external API documentation for its maximum payload or file size limit
Estimate the actual payload size being sent — base64-encoded content is approximately 33% larger than the original binary size
Check Make's own file size limits in Make's current documentation (limits may change with platform updates)
Determine whether the issue is file content size or JSON body size

solutions.solution: Upload large files to an intermediate cloud storage service (Google Drive, S3, Cloudinary) first, then pass the URL reference to the target API instead of the file content
solutions.conditions: When the target API accepts a file URL or supports downloading from a URL instead of receiving file content directly

solutions.solution: Implement pagination in the source data module to reduce the size of each individual API call
solutions.conditions: When a large JSON body can be split across multiple smaller paginated requests

prevention: Avoid routing binary file content through Make as base64 when URL references are supported by the target API
Check file size limits in both Make's platform documentation and the target API documentation before designing file transfer scenarios
